msContents.summary:
[p]Chirurgia, preceded by a work on Anatomy based on Mondeville and Lanfranc of Milan: in an incomplete and abridged English translation, originally written in 1392, by an unknown surgeon who seems to have practised in London. With medical notes and miscellaneous receipts by several late 15th cent. and early 16th cent. hands, also in English.[/p]
[p][u]Contents[/u][/p]
[p]ff. 1-9 blank[/p]
[p]1. ff. 10r Prologue[/p]
[p]Opens: 'The holi trinite that is heed and welle of knowynge...'[/p]
[p]Ends: '...it schal ben bi hem benygly fulfillid'.[/p]
[p]2. ff. 10r-55v First 'distinccioun'[/p]
[p]Opens: 'Here bigunneth the firste partie of this compilacioun where I have ordeyned the anothomy of a man...[/p]
[p]Ends: 'And thus endith this chapitre afornseid etc.'[/p]
[p]3. ff. 56r-124v Second 'distinccioun'[/p]
[p]Title: 'Now bigynneth the secunde partie of this compilacioun'[/p]
[p]Incipit: 'Where I have ordeyned the qualitees and the diffinicioun of a surgian...'[/p]
[p]Explicit: 'Here endith the first distinccioun of the firste partie. and thou schalt haue here next folowinge the secunde distinccioun of the secunde partie'[/p]
[p]4. ff. 124v-128r Second 'distinccioun' of the second part, incomplete.[/p]
[p]Incipit: 'In the secunde distinccioun of the secunde partie is ordeyned particuler woundis bigynnynge at the heed...'[/p]
[p]Ends imperfectly: '...whanne the pyement is clarified...'[/p]
[p]5. ff. 146r-170v A further section of this work[/p]
[p]Opens: 'The name of the tri nite thre personys and oo[n] god fadir and sone and ho ly goost. I thinke with the grace of god to dra / we out the general rulis or surgerie that bee moost nedeful to a surgian...'[/p]
[p]Ends: '...but if ther be a wounde in siche drie bodies and membris that gheuen superflue. Here ends the main work.'[/p]
[p]It seems probable that this MS. is a copy from an incomplete or partly illegible original: there are several gaps in the text, and the last part ends in the middle of a sentence.[/p]
[p]6. ff. 128v-130v Rough drawings in ink of urine flasks, with notes in English by a middle 16th cent. hand.[/p]
[p].7 ff. 131r-137r Alchemical, chemical and pharmaceutical notes in English by the same, or a similar hand.[/p]
[p]8. ff. 137v-139r Numeration from 1-1000 in English and Latin, and medical receipts in English.
[p]ff. 139v-143r blank[/p]
[p]9. ff. 143v-145v Notes on the humours, medical astrology, weights and measures, receipts, etc. by the earlier hand of Fol. 137v.[/p]
[p]10. ff. 171v-196r Medical receipts in English, contributed by several hands, including those of the writers of previous entries.[/p]
[p]196v-200r blank[/p]

msItem.author: Henri de Mondeville
msItem.title: Henri de Mondeville, [i]Chirurgia[/i], plus miscellaneous receipts
msItem.filiation: [p]Inserted is an envelope containing holograph notes on the anatomical part of this MS. by Joseph Frank Payne [1840-1910] (13 ll.). This MS. was the subject of an article by him in the [i]British Medical Journal[/i] 1896, i, pp. 200-203 entitled 'On an unpublished anatomical treatise of the fourteenth century, and its relation to the 'Anatomy' of Thomas Vicary'. Payne has also written a note on fol. 9v of the MS., with his signature, and address. This inscripton is found under the signature of H.W. Bailey of Thetford-a former owner (c. 1875). Book-plate of J. F. Payne. [p]Anglo Saxon letter forms in Moorat's catalogue description (such as contraction marks and Thorn and yogh symbols) have been replaced with Latin characters.

objectDesc.supportDesc:
1 volume201 ll. folio. 32 x 231/2 cm. 18th cent. panelled calf binding rebacked. A leaf has been cut out after fol. 9, and two leaves after fol. 142. Fol. 190 and fol. 191 were at one time pasted together, and have been damaged in separation with some loss of text: fol. 192 is also defective. There seems to have been some confusion in the re-binding of the last 10 ff. A few leaves with small defects, or stained. There is an original vellum fly-leaf at the end. Written in a large clear gothic hand in double column of 34 lines to a column. Large ornamental initials in red and black on ff. 10v, 16v, 47v, 56v, 124v, 146, other capitals, paragraph marks and underlinings in red. The 16th cent. pagination is confused, and the MS. has been refoliated in pencil at the lower outer margin.
This looks like it has been conserved at some point. Is in very good condition, no need at all to restrict. (AE, Oct 2011)
